#+TITLE: The input-output growth gap: a falsification chain
#+SUBTITLE: Locating the difference between deflated ICIO growth and official GDP growth
#+AUTHOR: G. Petrini
#+DATE: 2026-07-23
#+OPTIONS: toc:2 num:t
#+LATEX_HEADER: \usepackage{booktabs}

# Phase B write-up of the gap diagnosis (spec: gpetrini/PrivateClaude issue #7).
# House style: one sentence per line; no em-dashes; academic register; Org-mode.
# Every number is generated by code from archive/writeup_numbers.R; the prose cites no
# absolute value, so the text survives a re-estimation of the scripts.

* Abstract

The deflated OECD ICIO tables imply a measure of real GDP growth.
That measure differs from the official growth of the same aggregate.
This study locates the difference rather than assuming its source.
The analysis is organised as a falsification chain: each candidate source is stated as a prediction with a pre-registered decision rule, tested by a substitution through an accounting identity or by an external comparison, and assigned a verdict with an explicit confidence.
Two substitutable channels, the applied exchange rate and the applied GDP deflator, are rejected for the majority of countries.
The surviving majority difference is located in the ICIO nominal-dollar aggregate, which departs from official nominal GDP period by period.
A separate audit verifies that the input-output growth measure is computed correctly from the raw tables, so the residual is a property of the tables and not of the code.

* The object and the identity

Let $g^{IO}$ denote real GDP growth from the deflated ICIO tables and let $g^{off}$ denote official real GDP growth.
The object of study is the gap, defined once as
$$ \text{Gap} = g^{IO} - g^{off}, $$
measured in log growth per country-year.

The deflation applies one uniform scalar per country-year, the exchange rate over the GDP deflator, to every cell of the raw current-dollar table.
Because the aggregate is linear in components that all carry that scalar, the input-output growth measure satisfies the identity
$$ g^{IO} = \Delta\ln(\text{ICIO nominal, USD}) + \Delta\ln e - \pi, $$
where $e$ is the exchange rate and $\pi$ is deflator inflation.
The identity is the engine of the diagnosis.
It shows that the exchange rate, the deflator and official growth enter the gap as substitutable terms, so replacing any one of them recomputes the gap without re-running the pipeline.
The one term that is not substitutable through the identity is the ICIO nominal aggregate, which is reachable only by external comparison.

* The method rule

An identity does not attribute cause.
The size of a term says where the gap sits, not what produced it.
Every verdict in this study therefore rests on a substitution through the identity or on an external comparison against an independent series, never on the magnitude of a term alone.
This rule is what separates a location from an explanation, and it is applied uniformly to every hypothesis below.

* The quarantine

A minority of country-years reflects exogenous currency re-expression rather than measurement of growth.
These are redenominations, hyperinflation spikes and the pandemic year.
They are quarantined by an explicit classification, and every majority statistic reported below excludes the quarantined set.
Naming the partition makes the scope of every later claim exact.

#+begin_src R :session xrgap :results output latex :eval yes
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath("../../../archive"))
setwd(normalizePath("../../../archive"))
suppressMessages(source("writeup_numbers.R"))
cat(knitr::kable(wn_partition(), format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
  caption = "The majority and quarantine partition of the panel."))
#+end_src

The majority table fixes the denominator of every pooled statistic.
The quarantine is justified by the source of the movement, not by its size, so the exclusion is a statement about provenance rather than a trimming of outliers.

* The operational threshold

A gap is treated as closed when it falls below an operational threshold.
The threshold is set at the knee of the coverage curve, the point past which raising the tolerance buys little additional coverage.
Fixing it empirically makes the phrase "the gap is closed for the majority" a measured statement rather than an arbitrary one.

#+begin_src R :session xrgap :results output latex :eval yes
cat(knitr::kable(wn_coverage(), format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
  caption = "Coverage of the majority at the operational threshold: share of country-years and share of countries by median year."))
#+end_src

#+CAPTION: Coverage as a function of the gap threshold, with the knee that sets the operational value.
#+NAME: fig-coverage
[[file:../../../figs/gap_coverage_curve.pdf]]

The curve is read for its shape, not its level: coverage rises steeply until the knee and flattens after it, which is what makes the knee a defensible cut.

* H4: the exchange-rate channel

The prediction is that the applied exchange-rate series is the source of the majority gap.
The identity gives the test directly.
Substituting an independent World Bank exchange rate for the applied rate changes only $\Delta\ln e$, so the gap moves by exactly the difference of the two log changes.
The pre-registered rule rejects the hypothesis if the change in the mean absolute gap is small and establishes it if the change is large.

#+begin_src R :session xrgap :results output latex :eval yes
h4 <- wn_h4()
cat(knitr::kable(h4, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 4,
  caption = sprintf("H4 exchange-rate substitution. The reconversion filter removes %d euro-adoption break-years (%s), which are exogenous re-expressions, not exchange-rate movements.",
    attr(h4, "redenom_n"), attr(h4, "redenom_iso"))))
#+end_src

The raw pooled change is dominated by a handful of euro-adoption reconversion break-years in the substitute series, in which a national currency is re-expressed in euro.
These are the same exogenous re-expressions the quarantine removes, appearing here inside the substitute rather than the applied rate.
Once they are removed, the clean moved subset shows a change below the rejection threshold, and the substitution raises the gap rather than lowering it.
The applied exchange rate is therefore not the source of the majority gap.

* H2: the deflator channel

The prediction is that the applied GDP deflator is the source of the majority gap.
The identity again gives the test: substituting an independent deflator changes only $\pi$.
The report is country-level rather than pooled, because a pooled mean hides the distribution across countries.

#+begin_src R :session xrgap :results output latex :eval yes
h2 <- wn_h2()
cat(knitr::kable(h2$breakdown, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 1,
  caption = "H2 deflator substitution at the country level: how many countries improve, stay unchanged, or worsen under the swap."))
#+end_src

The large majority of countries are unchanged by the swap, a small number improve, and a small number worsen.
The countries that worsen are the highest-inflation cases, in which the two deflator series disagree on the annual timing of inflation rather than on its average level.

#+begin_src R :session xrgap :results output latex :eval yes
cat(knitr::kable(h2$named, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 2,
  caption = "The high-inflation deteriorations under the deflator swap, shown as a finding about annual timing disagreement rather than as noise."))
#+end_src

Because most countries are unchanged and the deteriorations are explained by timing disagreement in high-inflation cases, the applied deflator is not the source of the majority gap.
The four high-inflation countries are flagged for the volatile-country remediation, which is deferred, not resolved here.

* H1: the nominal aggregate

The two substitutable channels are rejected, so by elimination the surviving majority gap must sit in the one non-substitutable term, the ICIO nominal aggregate.
This is tested directly rather than by elimination alone.
The nominal aggregate is compared, in levels, against an independent World Bank current-dollar series of official nominal GDP.
The pre-registered rule confirms the location if the nominal term dominates the deflator term across the majority of country-years and if the gap is well approximated by the nominal term.

#+begin_src R :session xrgap :results output latex :eval yes
cat(knitr::kable(wn_h1(), format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
  caption = "H1 direct level test: the nominal-aggregate term dominates the gap and the ICIO nominal level tracks official nominal GDP for most countries."))
#+end_src

#+CAPTION: ICIO nominal-dollar level against official nominal GDP, normalised to a common base year, showing where the two nominal levels diverge.
#+NAME: fig-h1-levels
[[file:../../../figs/h1_nominal_level_divergence.pdf]]

The nominal term dominates the deflator term across the majority, and the two normalised nominal-dollar levels track for most countries, diverging only for a minority.
The residual majority gap is therefore the balanced ICIO nominal aggregate differing from official nominal GDP period by period.
It is bounded by the input-output tables and is not removable by any deflation or exchange-rate choice available on disk.

* H6: the benchmark vintage

The benchmark of official growth carries a vintage.
The difference between the vintage used and the current vintage of the same indicator is a bounded band in standard deviation.
This band is settled above the confidence bar and is attached as a caution to every country-level figure, so that no single country reading is over-interpreted.

* The pipeline-error audit

Every verdict above treats the identity as an exact property of the Stage-A pipeline.
That was verified only algebraically inside the decomposition code, never that the input-output growth measure is computed correctly from the tables.
A methodological error in the table-generating scripts, in the aggregation, or in the deflation would present exactly as the H1 residual.
The audit tests this assumption before the write-up asserts H1.

The assembly function that turns the supplied tables into the growth measure was verified in isolation, on a synthetic hand-computable fixture and by internal-consistency checks on the real tables.
The decisive test reconstructed the nominal-dollar aggregate independently from the raw tables, for every country-year, and closed the identity cell for cell against the deflated pipeline.

#+begin_src R :session xrgap :results output latex :eval yes
cat(knitr::kable(wn_audit(), format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
  caption = "The pipeline-error audit. The identity closes to machine precision, so the input-output growth measure is a faithful transform of the raw ICIO nominal aggregate."))
#+end_src

The identity closes to machine precision, orders of magnitude below the pre-registered tolerance.
The deflation is uniform per country-year, the aggregation and deflation compose correctly, and the recovered scalar equals the external exchange-rate over deflator ratio exactly on the country-years the OECD sources cover.
There is therefore no Stage-A or aggregation artifact masquerading as H1.
The residual is a property of the tables, and the H1 verdict rests on a verified pipeline rather than on an untested assumption.

* The falsification chain at a glance

#+begin_src R :session xrgap :results output latex :eval yes
cat(knitr::kable(wn_hyp_summary(), format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
  caption = "The falsification chain: each hypothesis as a prediction with a pre-registered decision rule, its verdict and its confidence."))
#+end_src

The table is the argument in one view.
Each row is a falsifiable prediction with a rule fixed before the result, so the logic can be checked independently of the outcome.

* Limits

Two limits bound the claims.
First, the level test locates the residual in the nominal aggregate but does not separate an inherited-table defect, in which the balanced ICIO tables differ from transcribed official nominal GDP, from a vintage artifact between the benchmark and the ICIO volumes.
The discriminating experiment is a current-vintage current-dollar series to replace the single benchmark file, which is a data fetch and is out of scope here.
Second, the volatile-country remediation for the high-inflation and volatile cases is deferred.
The pipeline verification itself holds for every country-year, including the quarantined minority, so the quarantine reflects input pathologies and never a computational defect.

The causal verdict is stated for the majority, the destination of the diagnosis.
The confidence on H1 is held at the confidence bar and not raised, because the audit removes a specific alternative but does not resolve the interpretive uncertainty that set the ceiling.
The evidence that would change the verdict is, in order of what it would move: a divergence between the raw tables and the published official nominal totals would reopen the pipeline finding; a vintage-matched current-dollar series that collapsed the divergence would reclassify the interpretation toward vintage; a re-estimated panel that moved the majority median gap or the coverage would move the magnitude of the account.

* Reproducibility

Every table in this document is generated by =archive/writeup_numbers.R=, which sources the audited diagnosis and retest scripts and returns each cited quantity, so no number is transcribed and a re-estimation propagates automatically.
The figures are the PDFs the diagnosis produced, reused without renaming.
The entry points are =archive/diagnose_xr_gap.R= for the panel and the identity, =archive/retest_h4_xr_swap.R=, =archive/retest_h2_deflator_swap.R= and =archive/retest_h1_nominal_levels.R= for the three substitution tests, and =archive/verify_prepare_data.R= with =archive/retest_h1_identity_closure.R= for the pipeline audit.
These scripts were moved from =code/= to =archive/= on 2026-08-04, when the gap was resolved upstream; they remain executable from inside =archive/=, see =archive/README.org=.
The full record is =docs/superpowers/findings/2026-07-21-xr-gap-diagnosis-findings.org=.
